newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent lower while feeder cattle were called steady, livestock analysts said.

The continued weak tone to the wholesale boxed beef market and expected slow fed cattle trade will likely weigh on live cattle futures. Boxed beef values were down to lowest levels since late September. Further weakness in pork pits could also spill over, analysts said.
However, expectations that demand for beef should start to improve for first of the month beef featuring could provide underlying support, they said.

Feeder cattle were expected to trade steady following the unchanged index and lower corn futures calls which should offset any spillover weakness from other meat pits. The improving feed situation should improve demand for feeders, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was unchanged at $63.04 per cwt.
Both pits will close early at noon CDT due to the Columbus Day holiday.
